scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-SLOW-TICKET-RESPONSE.statement: SH-CS frames the dispute surge as a ticket-handling capacity/response problem solvable by an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-fixes bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August caused incorrect acceptance/substitution of reads, producing systematically wrong bills.

H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE.statement: The AMI vendor's nightly MDMS export (H-MDMS-BILL) began failing or delivering incomplete/invalid AMI reads since August, forcing more estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-SHORTFALL.statement: MeterWorks field reading routes went incomplete or reads failed to upload since August, increasing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-ESTIMATE-SUBSTITUTION-SURGE.statement: Independent of which upstream read source failed, the estimate-substitution step itself increased in volume or error rate since August, directly driving wrong bills.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILLING-ERROR.statement: A majority of disputed bills (1785 of 3025) are billed on ACTUAL reads, suggesting a cause distinct from estimate substitution, such as incorrect acceptance or processing of actual reads in billing import, is driving most of the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field route-log data shows manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 at 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts — a measurable shortfall in completed field reads that could feed estimate substitution and wrong bills, but the magnitude relative to the dispute-ticket doubling is not yet established.

The billing-db tariff change log shows zero records, meaning no tariff changes were logged — this rules out a tariff/pricing change as a cause of the wrong bills driving the dispute surge, independent of the read-collection/validation causal chain already under investigation.

billing-db.disputed_bills_by_read_type (E-03) splits disputed bills by the read type billed: 1240 ESTIMATED and 1785 ACTUAL, so the majority (1785/3025, about 59%) of disputed bills were billed on ACTUAL reads, not substituted estimates. This caps how much of the dispute surge any estimate-substitution-driven cause (AMI export failure, field read shortfall, substitution surge) can explain, since those mechanisms only act on the ESTIMATED-read minority.

CRM dispute_response_times shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets — ticket handling is currently within SLA, so slow response capacity is not an active bottleneck. This weighs against framing the dispute surge as a response-speed/capacity problem and points attention back to bill correctness (read collection/import) as the surge driver.

E-05.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year, which echoes the direction of E-02 (billing-db tariff_change_log, 0 records for Aug-Sep). As an interview statement it is a non-authoritative claim, not new proof, but it does not introduce a tariff-change cause for the dispute surge.

CRM dispute_volume_monthly shows stable baseline volume in June-July (610, 590) followed by a jump to 1180 in August and 1260 in September — roughly a 2x increase that aligns with the timing claimed in the initial request. This confirms the magnitude and timing of the surge itself but says nothing about which upstream cause (read type, AMI export, field reads, billing rules, response capacity) drives it.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a staffing shortfall of three readers since July causes field routes to run late, forcing estimated billing for those customers — a candidate mechanism for the field route completion shortfall already shown in E-01/F-01 (0.88 vs 0.95 target). This is a non-authoritative interview statement from a stakeholder with a noted incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias (attributes problems to staffing), so it is a claim, not corroborated fact.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) confirms the utility (ORG-UTIL) may request field dispatch route priority changes, but execution happens only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) — this is the contractual basis for the already-recorded K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update, and bears on who may authorize a future route-change remediation, not on the dispute-surge root cause itself.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-09) shows 320 accounts across 40 routes were billed on estimated reads in the most recent cycle, but the returned fields (account_id, route only) contain no read-type, import-status or tariff data. So this query does not deliver the actual-read billing-import analysis that W-WI-ANALYZE-ACTUAL-READ-ERROR intended; it only yields a route-level distribution of currently estimated accounts.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-10) lists 14 specific lagging routes with completion values (sample: 0.70 for R-00), adding route-level granularity to the aggregate field completion shortfall already seen in E-01 (0.88 vs 0.95 target). The returned fields are limited to completion and route only, with no account-id, read-type, or dispute-ticket linkage, so this data cannot by itself correlate route lag with ESTIMATED-read disputes as W-WI-CORRELATE-ROUTE-ESTIMATED intended.

U-BILLING-IMPORT-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines whether remediation requires a billing-config rule fix or a different corrective action, and whether any bill-write/credit action under K-BILLWRITE is ever justified.
U-BILLING-IMPORT-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Query the billing-config rule change log (DA-RULES) for changes coinciding with August and cross-reference against disputed ACTUAL-read bills (E-03).
U-BILLING-IMPORT-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: No bill adjustments and no auto-fix agent; continue read-only investigation of billing-config.

U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION.question: How much of the ESTIMATED-read dispute minority (1240/3025) is attributable to the field reader staffing shortfall, and would correcting it require a dispatch route change?
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether a push_route_update (K-DISPATCH, protected action) is warranted as part of remediation scope.

U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: No field dispatch route changes proposed until the overlap is quantified.

U-MDMS-EXPORT-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Treat H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE as rejected per E-03 until new vendor data arrives.

U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Affects whether success criteria must also directly track the actual-read error rate in billing-db, not just ticket volume.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Track disputed_bills_by_read_type (DA-BILL) alongside dispute_volume_monthly to confirm both move together after remediation.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Report both metrics in parallel rather than relying on ticket volume alone.

A-READ-TYPE-SPLIT-MATCHES-SURG.statement: The ACTUAL/ESTIMATED read-type split of disputed bills (E-03) is assumed to apply to the same Aug-Sep surge population measured in E-06, not an unrelated historical sample.

A-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE-MECHANIS.statement: A billing import validation rule change (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE, CANDIDATE) is assumed to be a plausible proximate cause of the actual-read billing errors, pending an audit of DA-RULES.
